**Finding submitted: missing (insurance clause absent).**

- **Investigation:** A document-wide search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and there is no insurance heading in the section outline. I read the full General Matters block (§20 plus its continuation at p0141–p0147 and p0149) — it covers time of essence, notices, waiver, assignment, independent contractors, force majeure, severability, governing law, headings and entire agreement, but nothing on insurance.
- **Why the rule bites:** Garman is not a pure shrink-wrap licensor. It installs the Software at Authorized Locations and converts Sparkling's data (p0041–p0042), and provides on-site training and implementation support (§5, §9). That is a vendor touching both our data and our premises, so zero coverage sits in walk-away territory rather than merely below preferred.
- **Redline:** Inserted a new clause 20(k) after the entire-agreement paragraph at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). I placed it after p0149 rather than after p0147 because "(j)" is already used, so "(k)" keeps the lettering clean. The model language's "Customer Data" reference was adapted to "Sparkling's data" since this Agreement has no defined term "Customer Data" — it uses that phrasing in §4.
- The comment offers the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as a negotiating landing zone.
